newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong property frenzy turns violent.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong property frenzy turns violent.

text.p: Hong Kong's flat-buying frenzy turned violent for one property agent who was knocked unconscious at a flat sale, a local newspaper said on Friday.
Tempers flared on Thursday as security guards sought to control property agents trying to reach buyers queuing at a popular development and an agent was knocked out, the Tin Tin Daily News reported.
A police spokeswoman said two guards, aged 23 and 31, were arrested after the scuffle on Thursday and released on bail.
The altercation came a day after the government announced measures designed to bring flats on to the market more quickly in a bid to curb prices and speculation.
Hong Kong flat sales often draw hundreds of hopeful buyers for every unit on offer. Each potential buyer must register in a lottery to win a coupon entitling the owner to choose a flat.

The lucky winners are often besieged by property agents and mortgage lenders eager for their business. The coupons themselves, which merely ensure holders a place in the queue, have changed hands for as much as HK$1.5 million (US$192,000).
